questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

questions.q: Which gas is released when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to sodium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Carbonates react with acids to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Copper powder is heated in air in a china dish and it turns black. The black substance is
questions.explanation: Copper combines with oxygen to form black copper(II) oxide.

questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water is called
questions.explanation: This is a neutralisation reaction.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn + H2SO4 giving ZnSO4 + H2, which statement is correct?
options: It is a double displacement reaction
Zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal displaces hydrogen from the acid.

questions.q: In the balanced equation C2H5OH + 3O2 giving 2CO2 + yH2O, the value of y is
questions.explanation: Ethanol has 6 hydrogen atoms, so 3 water molecules are needed.

questions.q: What is a redox reaction?
questions.answer: A redox reaction is a reaction in which oxidation and reduction take place at the same time: one substance is oxidised while another is reduced.
keyPoints: One substance oxidised and another reduced
questions.explanation: For example, CuO + H2 gives Cu + H2O.

questions.q: Why does a copper vessel lose its shine and get a green coating when left in moist air?
questions.answer: Copper reacts slowly with moisture, carbon dioxide and oxygen in the air. This forms a green coating of basic copper carbonate, which is an example of corrosion.
questions.explanation: The metal is attacked by substances in the air.

questions.q: Which indicator turns pink in a basic solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acids and pink in bases.

questions.q: Milk of magnesia, used as an antacid, contains
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a mild base that neutralises stomach acid.

questions.q: A bee sting injects formic acid. Which of these can be rubbed on the sting to give relief?
questions.explanation: A mild base neutralises the acid, whereas the others are acidic.

questions.q: The chemical formula of sulphuric acid is
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid contains two hydrogen, one sulphur and four oxygen atoms.

questions.q: Acid solutions conduct electricity because they contain
questions.explanation: Acids form H+ ions and other ions in water.

questions.q: A milkman adds a little baking soda to fresh milk, and the milk takes longer to set as curd. The reason is that
options: the milk becomes slightly alkaline, so more acid must be produced to set it
baking soda kills all the bacteria
baking soda turns milk into water
questions.explanation: Baking soda raises the pH, and curd forms only after enough acid is produced.

questions.q: Name the products formed when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate.
questions.answer: A salt, water and carbon dioxide gas are formed.
questions.explanation: For example, Na2CO3 + 2HCl gives 2NaCl + H2O + CO2.

questions.q: Why does an aqueous solution of an acid conduct electricity while a glucose solution does not?
questions.answer: Acids split into ions (such as H+) in water, and these moving ions carry current. Glucose contains hydrogen but does not form ions in water, so its solution does not conduct.
questions.explanation: Conduction needs free ions.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most malleable metal?
questions.explanation: Gold can be beaten into extremely thin sheets.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
questions.explanation: Potassium is high in the reactivity series.

questions.q: A copper strip placed in iron sulphate solution shows no change because
options: copper is more reactive than iron
copper is less reactive than iron and cannot displace it
questions.explanation: Only a more reactive metal can displace another from its salt.

questions.q: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only liquid non-metal.

questions.q: Solder, used for welding electrical wires, is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Solder is lead and tin and has a low melting point.

questions.q: Iron objects near the sea coast rust faster mainly because
options: salts in the moist air speed up corrosion
questions.explanation: Dissolved salts make the moisture a better conductor and speed up rusting.

questions.q: What is meant by the reactivity series of metals?
questions.answer: The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their reactivity, from the most reactive, such as potassium, to the least reactive, such as gold.
keyPoints: Order from most to least reactive
questions.explanation: It predicts which metal can displace another.

questions.q: Differentiate between roasting and calcination.
questions.answer: In roasting, a sulphide ore is heated strongly in excess of air to form the oxide. In calcination, a carbonate ore is heated strongly in limited air or no air to form the oxide.
keyPoints: Roasting for sulphide ores in excess air
Calcination for carbonate ores in limited air
questions.explanation: Both convert the ore into a metal oxide.

questions.q: The chemical name of CH3CH2OH is
questions.explanation: A two-carbon alcohol is ethanol.

questions.q: The number of carbon atoms in a molecule of propane is
questions.explanation: The prefix prop- means three carbons.

questions.q: The number of hydrogen atoms in a molecule of pentane (C5H12) is
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the formula CnH(2n+2), so for n = 5 it is 12.

questions.q: The burning of carbon compounds in oxygen with the release of heat and light is called
questions.explanation: Combustion is rapid oxidation with heat and light.

questions.q: Ethanol is oxidised by alkaline potassium permanganate to give
questions.explanation: Oxidising agents convert ethanol to ethanoic acid.

questions.q: Detergents are better than soaps for washing in hard water because
options: their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble, so no scum forms
questions.explanation: Detergents do not form insoluble scum with the ions of hard water.

questions.q: What is a functional group? Give two examples.
questions.answer: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms in a carbon compound that decides its chemical properties. Examples are -OH (alcohol) and -COOH (carboxylic acid).
keyPoints: Atom or group deciding chemical properties
questions.explanation: Compounds with the same functional group react similarly.

questions.q: Why are carbon compounds generally poor conductors of electricity?
questions.answer: Carbon compounds are formed by sharing of electrons, so they are made of neutral molecules and have no free ions or electrons to carry current.
questions.explanation: Conduction needs charged particles that can move.

questions.q: Most of the digested food is absorbed in the
questions.explanation: The small intestine has villi and a rich blood supply for absorption.

questions.q: The red pigment in red blood cells is
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin binds oxygen and gives blood its red colour.

questions.q: During heavy exercise the breathing rate increases because
options: muscle cells need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: A faster rate supplies oxygen and removes extra carbon dioxide.

questions.q: The windpipe is also called the
questions.explanation: The trachea is held open by rings of cartilage.

questions.q: In pulmonary circulation, blood is taken from the heart to the
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation links the heart and the lungs.

questions.q: Transport of sugars in the phloem (translocation) differs from transport of water in the xylem in that it
options: is a passive process by gravity only
uses energy to move sucrose into the phloem tissue
questions.explanation: Sucrose is loaded into phloem using energy from ATP.

questions.q: What are enzymes?
questions.answer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly proteins, that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms. For example, amylase digests starch.
keyPoints: Speed up reactions in the body
questions.explanation: Digestive enzymes break food down into small molecules.

questions.q: How are oxygen and carbon dioxide exchanged in the alveoli?
questions.answer: The alveoli have very thin walls surrounded by capillaries. Oxygen from the air in the alveoli diffuses into the blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli to be breathed out.
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs by diffusion.

questions.q: The pituitary is often called the master gland because it
questions.explanation: Pituitary hormones control other glands and body growth.

questions.q: A reflex arc consists of a receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron and an
questions.explanation: The effector, a muscle or gland, produces the response.

questions.q: The pollen tube grows towards the ovule in response to chemicals. This movement is called
questions.explanation: Growth towards a chemical stimulus is chemotropism.

questions.q: The plant hormone that helps in the ripening of fruits is
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous hormone for fruit ripening.

questions.q: Cytokinins mainly promote
questions.explanation: Cytokinins are found in rapidly dividing tissues like fruits and seeds.

questions.q: Animals use both nerves and hormones for control because
options: nerves can work only in the brain
nerve impulses are fast and short-lived, whereas hormones act more slowly and their effects last longer
questions.explanation: The two systems complement each other.

questions.q: State the function of the cerebellum.
questions.answer: The cerebellum maintains the posture and balance of the body and coordinates voluntary movements such as walking in a straight line or picking up a pencil.
questions.explanation: It is part of the hindbrain.

questions.q: Compare nervous control and hormonal control in animals.
questions.answer: Nervous control uses electrical impulses that travel along nerves and give quick, short-lived responses. Hormonal control uses chemicals carried by blood, which act more slowly but have longer-lasting effects.
keyPoints: Hormonal: chemicals in blood, slower, long-lasting
questions.explanation: The two systems work together.

questions.q: A potato plant is grown commonly from its
questions.explanation: Each eye on a potato tuber can grow into a new plant.

questions.q: In human males, sperms are produced in the
questions.explanation: The testes make sperm and the hormone testosterone.

questions.q: Reproduction is essential for a species, though not for the survival of an individual, because it
options: increases the lifespan of the individual
maintains the continuity of the species
questions.explanation: Without reproduction the species would die out as individuals die.

questions.q: The release of an egg from the ovary is called
questions.explanation: Ovulation is release of a mature egg.

questions.q: The normal period of pregnancy in humans is about
questions.explanation: The gestation period is about nine months.

questions.q: Wind-pollinated flowers usually produce
options: light, dry pollen in very large quantities
questions.explanation: Large quantities of light pollen improve the chance of reaching a stigma.

questions.q: What is regeneration? Name an organism that shows it.
questions.answer: Regeneration is the ability of an organism to grow back lost parts or even a whole new individual from a piece. Planaria and Hydra show regeneration.
keyPoints: Example such as Planaria or Hydra
questions.explanation: Specialised cells make new tissues.

questions.q: How does the male gamete reach the egg in a flower after the pollen lands on the stigma?
questions.answer: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube through the style down to the ovary. The male gamete passes through the tube to the ovule, where it fuses with the egg cell.
keyPoints: Pollen tube grows through the style
Reaches the ovule in the ovary
questions.explanation: This completes fertilisation in flowers.

questions.q: The genetic material in a cell is found mainly on the
questions.explanation: Genes are located on chromosomes in the nucleus.

questions.q: Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed. The chance that an offspring is dwarf is
questions.explanation: Only tt plants are dwarf, and they form one in four.

questions.q: Two tall pea plants produce some dwarf offspring. The genotypes of the parents must be
questions.explanation: Both must carry the recessive allele to produce tt offspring, and they are tall, so both are Tt.

questions.q: Which process introduces small errors that cause variation?
questions.explanation: Inexact copying of DNA gives rise to variations.

questions.q: A pair of contrasting forms of a gene is called
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene, such as T and t.

questions.q: A Tt pea plant is tall although it carries the t allele because
options: the t allele makes the plant tall
the dominant T masks the effect of t
questions.explanation: A dominant allele shows its effect even when only one copy is present.

questions.q: What is meant by variation?
questions.answer: Variation means the differences between the individuals of a species, such as in height, colour or other characteristics.
questions.explanation: Variation arises from sexual reproduction and errors in DNA copying.

questions.q: Why was the garden pea a good choice for Mendel's experiments?
questions.answer: It has many easily seen contrasting traits, a short life cycle, produces many seeds, and can be self-pollinated or cross-pollinated in a controlled way.
keyPoints: Short life cycle and many seeds
questions.explanation: These features made the results easy to study.

questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300 000 km per second in vacuum.

questions.q: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is given by
questions.explanation: m = h'/h = -v/u.

questions.q: An object is placed beyond 2F of a convex lens. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F
at the focus and highly diminished
questions.explanation: For an object beyond 2F, the image lies between F and 2F on the other side.

questions.q: Which mirror has its principal focus behind the mirror?
questions.explanation: Reflected rays from a convex mirror appear to come from a point behind it.

questions.q: A ray of light enters a glass slab from air along the normal. It
questions.explanation: A ray along the normal is not deviated.

questions.q: Refractive indices are about 1.33 for water, 1.5 for glass and 2.42 for diamond. Light travels slowest in
questions.explanation: The higher the refractive index, the slower the light.

questions.q: What is meant by magnification? Write the formula for a mirror.
questions.answer: Magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, showing how much larger or smaller the image is. For a mirror, m = h'/h = -v/u.
keyPoints: Ratio of image height to object height
questions.explanation: A negative sign means a real, inverted image.

questions.q: State two differences between a real image and a virtual image.
questions.answer: A real image can be obtained on a screen, while a virtual image cannot. A real image is formed when light rays actually meet and is usually inverted, whereas a virtual image is formed by rays that only appear to meet and is erect.
keyPoints: Real image can be caught on a screen
Real is formed by actual meeting of rays
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether the rays actually meet.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The optic nerve carries signals from the retina to the
questions.explanation: The brain interprets the electrical signals as an image.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: To see a rainbow, the Sun must be
questions.explanation: Light from behind the observer is dispersed by raindrops in front.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Which of the following is not mainly due to scattering of light?
questions.explanation: A rainbow is caused by refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in water drops.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The defect in which distant objects appear blurred is
questions.explanation: Myopia means a person sees near objects clearly but not distant ones.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: When we look at a distant object, the ciliary muscles
options: contract and the lens becomes thicker
contract and the lens becomes thinner
relax and the lens becomes thicker
relax and the lens becomes thinner
questions.explanation: A thin lens has a longer focal length and focuses distant objects.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: A rectangular glass slab does not produce a spectrum from white light because
options: the opposite faces are parallel, so the dispersed colours recombine
the glass absorbs all the colours
light does not refract in glass
the slab is too thin to bend light
questions.explanation: The second parallel face bends the colours back, so the emergent beam is white again.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is the function of the optic nerve?
questions.answer: The optic nerve carries the electrical signals produced in the retina to the brain, where they are interpreted as images.
questions.explanation: Seeing is completed in the brain.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is hypermetropia? State one cause.
questions.answer: Hypermetropia is a defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly but not nearby ones, since the image forms behind the retina. It is caused by a weak eye lens with a long focal length or an eyeball that is too short.
keyPoints: A cause such as a short eyeball
questions.explanation: A convex lens corrects it.

questions.q: A device used to change the resistance in a circuit is called a
questions.explanation: A rheostat is a variable resistor.

questions.q: Four resistors of 2 ohm each are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 4 x 2 = 8 ohm.

questions.q: A 6 V battery is connected to a 4 ohm and a 2 ohm resistor in series. The potential difference across the 4 ohm resistor is
questions.explanation: The current is 6/6 = 1 A, so V = 1 x 4 = 4 V.

questions.q: Electric current in a metal wire is due to the flow of
questions.explanation: Free electrons carry the charge in metals.

questions.q: The heat produced when 2 A flows through a 5 ohm resistor for 10 s is
questions.explanation: H = I squared x R x t = 4 x 5 x 10 = 200 J.

questions.q: The fuse wire is made of an alloy with a low melting point so that
options: it can carry a very large current
it melts quickly and breaks the circuit when the current is too high
questions.explanation: A fuse melts if the current exceeds the safe value, protecting the appliances.

questions.q: State Joule's law of heating.
questions.answer: The heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current, to its resistance and to the time for which the current flows: H = I squared x R x t.
questions.explanation: This is the heating effect of electric current.

questions.q: Why does the filament of a bulb glow while the copper wires connected to it do not?
questions.answer: The filament has a very high resistance, so a lot of heat is produced in it by the same current and it becomes white hot. The connecting copper wires have very low resistance, so very little heat is produced in them.
keyPoints: More heat for the same current
questions.explanation: Heat is proportional to resistance for the same current.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic field strength is the
questions.explanation: Magnetic field strength is measured in tesla.

questions.q: The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire are
questions.explanation: The field lines form concentric circles around the wire.

questions.q: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field depends on
options: only the resistance of the wire
the current, the strength of the field and the length of conductor in the field
questions.explanation: The force is proportional to the current, the field and the length in the field.

questions.q: A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped in the shape of a cylinder is called a
questions.explanation: A solenoid behaves like a bar magnet when current flows through it.

questions.q: In domestic circuits in India, the potential difference between the live wire and the neutral wire is
questions.explanation: The supply voltage is 220 V.

questions.q: The direction of the induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of induced current.

questions.q: What is a solenoid? Describe the magnetic field inside it.
questions.answer: A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated wire wrapped like a cylinder. When current flows, the field inside it is uniform and parallel to the axis, and the coil acts like a bar magnet.
keyPoints: Coil of many turns shaped like a cylinder
questions.explanation: A soft iron core inside makes an electromagnet.

questions.q: Write two differences between alternating current and direct current.
questions.answer: Direct current flows in one direction only, while alternating current reverses its direction periodically. AC is supplied to homes by power stations and can be sent over long distances with less loss, while DC is obtained from cells and batteries.
keyPoints: DC one direction and AC reverses periodically
Sources: batteries for DC and generators for AC
questions.explanation: AC is preferred for long-distance transmission.

questions.q: Which of the following is a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Fungi break down dead matter.

questions.q: Herbivores belong to which trophic level?
questions.explanation: Producers are the first level and herbivores the second.

questions.q: An ecosystem needs a continuous supply of energy from the Sun because
options: energy flows in one direction and a lot is lost as heat at each step
questions.explanation: Energy is not recycled, so it must be renewed.

questions.q: A molecule of ozone contains how many oxygen atoms?
questions.explanation: Ozone is O3, while ordinary oxygen is O2.

questions.q: Biodegradable kitchen waste can be turned into manure by
questions.explanation: Composting lets microbes convert it into manure.

questions.q: For the same area of producers, a person who eats plant food gets more energy than one who eats meat because
options: less energy is lost, as fewer trophic levels are involved
questions.explanation: At each trophic level about 90 percent of energy is lost.

questions.q: Give two examples of natural ecosystems and two of man-made ecosystems.
questions.answer: Natural ecosystems: forest and pond (or ocean). Man-made ecosystems: crop field and aquarium (or garden).
questions.explanation: Man-made ecosystems are created and maintained by people.

questions.q: Suggest two ways to reduce waste at home.
questions.answer: Reduce the use of items such as plastic bags, reuse things like containers and bottles, and recycle paper, glass and metal. Kitchen waste can also be composted.
questions.explanation: These are the three Rs of waste management.
